--- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - zh library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: text-generation tags: - llm - nanbeige base_model: - Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B --- # Nanbeige4.3-33B-INT4 This repository contains the INT4 quantized version of [Nanbeige4.3-33B](https://huggingface.co/Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B). To preserve performance at 4-bit precision, we apply quantization-aware training (QAT), including on-policy distillation (OPD) from the BF16 model to the INT4 model and reinforcement learning (RL) on the INT4 model itself. # 1. Introduction In Nanbeige4.3, we take a foundational step toward pushing the boundaries of lightweight agents. Our strategy centers on building a high-capacity teacher agent first, which will subsequently anchor the distillation of advanced agentic capabilities into smaller models. To this end, we first introduce Nanbeige4.3-33B, designed as the flagship teacher model for the Nanbeige4.3 series. Delivering state-of-the-art agentic performance among open models in the ~30B parameter class, Nanbeige4.3-33B excels at complex coding and professional cowork tasks. It not only offers a powerful, cost-effective option for immediate real-world deployment, but also lays the necessary foundation to power our upcoming small model distillation pipeline (e.g., for Nanbeige4.3-3B). # 2. Model Performance The following BF16 results compare Nanbeige4.3-33B with recently released frontier models at around the 30B-parameter scale: Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B, and Gemma4-31B. All models are evaluated at their highest thinking effort. For each benchmark, we use the same inference hyperparameters and harness across models.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
project(xenithium VERSION 0.0.1 LANGUAGES CXX)

# Xenithium: native C++20 inference engine for Intel Arc Pro B-series (Battlemage, Xe2).
# SYCL (icpx, AOT for bmg) + ESIMD for kernels, Level Zero directly for memory and queues,
# no oneCCL. Multi-model: model-specific code lives in src/arch/<id>/.

if(NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "IntelLLVM")
  message(FATAL_ERROR "xenithium needs icpx (oneAPI DPC++), got ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID}")
endif()

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)
# No linker dependency files: under -fsycl the driver links temporary device objects ($TMPDIR/icpx-*/...o) that
# the linker records in link.d and then deletes, so every SYCL target looked out of date and every build (even a
# no-op) relinked all of them, AOT device compile included (~55 s, 5 CPU-minutes).
set(CMAKE_LINK_DEPENDS_USE_LINKER OFF)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
endif()

set(XENITHIUM_SYCL_TARGET "spir64_gen" CACHE STRING "SYCL AOT target")
set(XENITHIUM_SYCL_DEVICE "bmg" CACHE STRING "AOT device (bmg = Battlemage)")
option(XENITHIUM_BUILD_TESTS "Build the gates" ON)
# Device-code AOT at link time runs one backend compile per split module; serially that was ~29 s of every probe /
# server link, 8.8 s with 16 jobs (the same device images).
set(XENITHIUM_LINK_JOBS "16" CACHE STRING "parallel device-code compiles per SYCL link")

find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
find_package(LevelZero CONFIG QUIET)

# AOT: no JIT at start-up. The backend arguments are separate argv entries; one string with
# an embedded space is re-split by the Makefile generator and swallows the next flag.
set(XENITHIUM_SYCL_FLAGS
    -fsycl
    "-fsycl-targets=${XENITHIUM_SYCL_TARGET}"
    "-Xsycl-target-backend=${XENITHIUM_SYCL_TARGET}"
    "-device ${XENITHIUM_SYCL_DEVICE}"
    -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter)

# Every target that includes a SYCL / Level Zero header needs this itself: linking a SYCL
# library does not propagate the flags.
function(xenithium_configure target)
  target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE ${XENITHIUM_SYCL_FLAGS})
  target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE ${XENITHIUM_SYCL_FLAGS} -fsycl-max-parallel-link-jobs=${XENITHIUM_LINK_JOBS})
  target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)
  if(LevelZero_FOUND)
    target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE LevelZero::ze_loader)
  else()
    target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE ze_loader)
  endif()
endfunction()

# Host-only code: no -fsycl. icpx defaults to fast math for host code too, so precise
# floating point is requested explicitly (host references must round like IEEE).
function(xenithium_host target)
  target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)
  target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -O2 -Wall -Wextra -fp-model=precise)
endfunction()

# ---- host libraries --------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(xenithium_util STATIC src/util/json.cpp src/util/http.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_util)

# Text: the BPE tokenizer (generic over tokenizer.json) and each arch's chat format
# (template + output parser) behind text::ChatFormat.
add_library(xenithium_text STATIC src/text/tokenizer.cpp src/text/unicode.cpp src/text/chat_registry.cpp
            src/arch/qwen38/chat.cpp src/text/json_constraint.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_text)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_text PUBLIC xenithium_util)

# Serving layer, host only: the core's engine interface, admission, host sampler, the stub
# engine, and the OpenAI-compatible HTTP server.
add_library(xenithium_serve STATIC src/core/engine.cpp src/core/sampler.cpp src/core/stub_engine.cpp src/core/batch_engine.cpp
            src/server/http.cpp src/server/server.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_serve)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_serve PUBLIC xenithium_text Threads::Threads)

# Eval: per-position log-prob records (XLP1) and the KL gate against a reference dump.
add_library(xenithium_eval STATIC src/eval/logprobs.cpp src/eval/reference.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_eval)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_eval PUBLIC xenithium_util)

# Model layer: checkpoint catalog, config, the arch registry and every arch module.
# Weight packers and exact CPU references: host code shared by kernels, loader and tests.
add_library(xenithium_pack STATIC src/kernels/pack.cpp src/kernels/qsa_ref.cpp src/kernels/ple_ref.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_pack)

add_library(xenithium_model STATIC
  src/model/checkpoint.cpp
  src/model/bulk_read.cpp
  src/model/row_reader.cpp
  src/arch/qwen38/experts.cpp
  src/model/config.cpp
  src/model/registry.cpp
  src/arch/qwen38/arch.cpp
  src/arch/qwen35/arch.cpp
  src/arch/qwen38/ple_table.cpp
  src/arch/qwen38/mtp.cpp)
xenithium_host(xenithium_model)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_model PUBLIC xenithium_util xenithium_pack Threads::Threads)

# ---- device libraries ------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(xenithium_rt STATIC src/rt/l0.cpp src/rt/device.cpp src/rt/fabric.cpp)
xenithium_configure(xenithium_rt)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_rt PUBLIC Threads::Threads)

# Kernels that need 256 GRF (QsaScoreK measured no gain). The grf_size<256> kernel property does not reach ESIMD
# kernels under AOT (every kernel compiled at 128 GRF), so these live in a shared library whose
# device image is compiled with -doubleGRF; the static kernels keep 128 GRF. Only kernels that spill
# at 128 belong here: at 256 a kernel gets half the threads per EU, and the prefill's non-spilling
# kernels lost 11 % of 8K prefill there.
add_library(xenithium_kernels_xl SHARED src/kernels/gdn_scan.cpp src/kernels/moe_rows_gu.cpp src/kernels/w4a16_rows.cpp src/kernels/gqa_rows.cpp
            src/kernels/gqa_staged.cpp src/kernels/gqa_fa.cpp src/kernels/gqa_seg.cpp src/kernels/gdn_core8.cpp)
target_compile_options(xenithium_kernels_xl PRIVATE ${XENITHIUM_SYCL_FLAGS})
target_link_options(xenithium_kernels_xl PRIVATE -fsycl -fsycl-max-parallel-link-jobs=${XENITHIUM_LINK_JOBS} "-fsycl-targets=${XENITHIUM_SYCL_TARGET}"
                    "-Xsycl-target-backend=${XENITHIUM_SYCL_TARGET}" "-device ${XENITHIUM_SYCL_DEVICE} -options -doubleGRF")
target_include_directories(xenithium_kernels_xl PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)

add_library(xenithium_kernels STATIC src/kernels/int8_gemm.cpp src/kernels/w4a16_gemm.cpp src/kernels/dense.cpp
            src/kernels/hc.cpp src/kernels/hc_fused.cpp src/kernels/head.cpp src/kernels/moe.cpp
            src/kernels/wire.cpp src/kernels/gdn.cpp src/kernels/qsa.cpp src/kernels/ple.cpp src/kernels/mtp.cpp
            src/kernels/pf_dense.cpp src/kernels/moe_rows.cpp src/kernels/gdn_rows.cpp src/kernels/logprob.cpp
            src/kernels/rmsnorm.cpp src/kernels/mlp.cpp src/kernels/gqa.cpp src/kernels/gqa_sel.cpp src/kernels/dflash.cpp src/kernels/kv_copy.cpp)
xenithium_configure(xenithium_kernels)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_kernels PUBLIC xenithium_rt xenithium_pack xenithium_kernels_xl)

# Model modules that touch the cards (placement, loaders): SYCL + the host model layer.
add_library(xenithium_arch STATIC src/arch/qwen38/expert_store.cpp src/arch/qwen38/head.cpp src/arch/qwen38/hc.cpp src/arch/qwen38/moe.cpp src/arch/qwen38/gdn.cpp
            src/arch/qwen38/qsa.cpp src/arch/qwen38/ple.cpp src/arch/qwen38/model.cpp src/arch/qwen38/drafter.cpp src/arch/qwen38/prefill.cpp src/arch/qwen38/prefix.cpp
            src/arch/qwen35/head.cpp src/arch/qwen35/mlp.cpp src/arch/qwen35/gdn.cpp src/arch/qwen35/attn.cpp src/arch/qwen35/model.cpp src/arch/qwen35/mtp.cpp src/arch/qwen35/dflash.cpp src/arch/head_cands.cpp src/load/dense_store.cpp)
xenithium_configure(xenithium_arch)
target_link_libraries(xenithium_arch PUBLIC xenithium_rt xenithium_model xenithium_kernels)

# The serving engine's model adapters: core:StepModel over each arch's M

cases.text:
# The launcher: `scripts/launch.sh`

A full-screen terminal interface for `xenithium-server`: pick a model, edit the `server.env`
settings with their documentation beside them, see the exact command `scripts/start-server.sh`
will run, launch it, and watch the server load and serve.

    scripts/build-host.sh xenithium-launch    # once (host only, no GPU code; a few seconds)
    scripts/launch.sh                         # opens ./server.env
    scripts/launch.sh --env profiles/long.env # another settings file
    scripts/launch.sh --check                 # no screen: catalog and the file's invalid settings

It needs a terminal of at least 64 x 18 (100 columns or more puts the help beside the list), and
uses truecolor when `COLORTERM` says so, else 256 colours; `NO_COLOR` turns colours off. The theme is royal blue (frames, tabs, the chosen option, panels); orange, green, yellow and red keep their meaning (changed, ok, warning, error). The mouse
works (click a setting, click it again to edit, wheel to scroll, click a tab).

## Screens

**Configure** (`1`)

- the model card: the checkpoint, its arch (`qwen38` / `qwen35`, from the engine's own arch
  registry), size on disk, and whether speculative decoding is on. `m` opens the model list:
  every directory under `~/models` with a `config.json` (`--models DIR` for another place), grouped
  by arch, MTP and DFlash drafter directories left out, checkpoints the engine does not serve greyed;
  type to filter, or "Other directory" for any path (Tab completes).
- the settings, grouped in the order you decide them (model and network, capacity, speculative
  decoding, prefill scheduling, numerics, queue, runtime, diagnostics). Only the settings the
  server reads for this model are listed. The drafter settings offer their checkpoints as
  choices (the MTP ones named after the target, the DFlash ones under the models directory);
  `Other path` takes a free one. Hidden (`a` shows them, marked n/a): the other arch's
  settings, a setting whose switch is off (draft vocabulary with the drafter off, SJF aging unless
  the queue policy is sjf, VRAM reserve for `qwen35` unless the KV pool is `auto`), and, with the
  stub engine on, everything the stub does not read. A launch passes the hidden ones at their default. A value that differs from the default is orange, an invalid one red
  with the reason in the help panel, and `●` marks a setting changed since the file was opened.
- the help panel: the setting's key and flag, value, default, which arch reads it, the allowed
  values or range, and a laconic description of what it does: the measured effect and the cost.
  The full row with its history and measurements stays in `docs/server-env.md` (find searches it).
- the command: what `scripts/start-server.sh` prints with `SERVE_DRY_RUN=1` for the current values,
  refreshed on every change, with the script's own warnings (a missing hot-rank file, ...).

**Server** (`2`)

- the state: loading (time and the log's last line), READY with the URL (the LAN address when the
  server listens on `0.0.0.0`), stopping, or exited with its status.
- live numbers from `/metrics` once ready, on two lines. Now: requests running / slots, waiting,
  decode tok/s of the whole server (the tokens of all requests together over the last ~6 s, polled
  every second), per stream (that over the requests running), the peak since the server was seen,
  and for `qwen35` the KV pool use. Since the server started: requests done, tokens decoded and
  prefilled over all requests, and for `qwen35` the preemptions.
- the GPUs, one row: each card's board power now (its energy counter over the last second, from
  the xe driver's hwmon files; no root), its power limit and package temperature. The total is
  also in the top bar. Read-only: the launcher does not change power limits.
- the server's log, following its end (`↑` / PgUp scroll back, `End` follows again, `w` wraps).

## Keys

| key | does |
| --- | --- |
| `↑` `↓` / `j` `k`, PgUp PgDn, Home End | move |
| `Enter` | edit: a popup for choices and suggestions, a line editor for the rest; fold a group |
| `←` `→` / `h` `l` | previous / next choice (or suggestion) in place; fold / unfold a group |
| `Space` | toggle on / off, next choice |
| `e` (F2) | type a custom value; `Tab` completes paths, `Ctrl-U` clears, `Esc` cancels |
| `d` / `D` | this setting / every setting back to the default of `start-server.sh` |
| `u` | undo |
| `/` | find a setting by name, key or flag; with no name match it searches the help text |
| `m` | the model list |
| `p` | settings files: `server.env` and the profiles; `n` saves the current values as a new profile, `x` deletes one |
| `s` / `S` | save to the open file / save as (`server.env`, a profile, a new profile) |
| `r` (F5) | launch, after the checks |
| `x` | stop the server (SIGTERM; after 5 s of stopping, `x` offers SIGKILL) |
| `Tab`, `1` `2` | switch screens |
| `?` | keys |
| `q` | quit; with unsaved changes it asks first. A running server keeps running |

## Files

- `server.env` (repo root): what `scripts/start-server.sh` reads. Saving writes only the settings
  that differ from the script's defaults, updates them in place and keeps comments and other
  lines; a setting set back to its default is removed from the file.
- `profiles/NAME.env`: named settings files in the same format (`p` to open, `n` to create).
  `scripts/start-server.sh` reads one with `SERVE_ENV=profiles/NAME.env`.
- `build/launch/`: `launch.env` (the values of the last launch, every setting written out),
  `server.log` (its output; the one before is `server.log.1`), `server.pid`, `preview.env`.

Both `server.env` and `profiles/` are local files (`.gitignore`).

## Launching

`r` first checks, and shows each check: the server binary is built, the model is a checkpoint
the engine serves, every setting is valid (a `qwen35` context must fit the checkpoint's
`max_position_embeddings`, it has no YaRN yet; `qwen38` goes past it), the port is free, no Docker container holds the cards
(skipped for the stub engine), and whether unsaved values are being launched (they are launched
as shown; the file is not changed). It refuses while any `xenithium-server` runs.

The launch writes `build/launch/launch.env` and runs `SERVE_ENV=build/launch/launch.env
scripts/start-server.sh` in its own session, output to `build/launch/server.log`. The script's own
checks and defaults apply as for a launch by hand, and the command is the one shown under Command.
Settings the model's arch ignores are launched at their default (`--hot-rank` is left off for
`qwen35`). The server outlives the launcher: quitting prints its pid and URL, and the next
`scripts/launch.sh` finds it again (`build/launch/server.pid`) with its log. A server started by
hand is shown too (state, metrics, stop), without a log.

## Where the settings come from

The launcher does not keep its own copy of the defaults or the long help text: they are read at start
from `scripts/start-server.sh` (the `XEN_X=${XEN_X:-default}` lines) and `docs/server-env.md`
(the setting table and the diagnostic switches table). Its schema in `tools/launch/settings.cpp`
adds the label, group, type, allowed values, which arch reads each setting and a short description (`brief_of`, which must be rewritten when a setting's behaviour changes; the `launch` gate fails when one is missing). `unused_reason` holds the rules that hide a setting for the model and the current values. A setting the
script or docs have and the schema does not still appears, as text under "Other"; `--check` and
the `launch` gate (`xenithium-test-launch`) report any mismatch between the three. Adding or
renaming a `server.env` setting therefore also means a line in `schema()`.

## Code

`tools/launch/`: `term` (terminal: raw mode, alternate screen, diff rendering, key and mouse
decoding; no curses), `settings` (catalog, env files, validation, model scan), `proc` (dry run,
spawn, process and port checks, Docker, me

  every directory under `~/models` with a `config.json` (`--models DIR` for another place), grouped
  by arch, MTP and DFlash drafter directories left out, checkpoints the engine does not serve greyed;
  type to filter, or "Other directory" for any path (Tab completes).

  decoding, prefill scheduling, numerics, queue, runtime, diagnostics). Only the settings the
  server reads for this model are listed. The drafter settings offer their checkpoints as
  choices (the MTP ones named after the target, the DFlash ones under the models directory);
  `Other path` takes a free one. Hidden (`a` shows them, marked n/a): the other arch's
  settings, a setting whose switch is off (draft vocabulary with the drafter off, SJF aging unless
  the queue policy is sjf, VRAM reserve for `qwen35` unless the KV pool is `auto`), and, with the
  stub engine on, everything the stub does not read. A launch passes the hidden ones at their default. A value that differs from the default is orange, an invalid one red

  values or range, and a laconic description of what it does: the measured effect and the cost.

  server listens on `0.0.0.0`), stopping, or exited with its status.

  prefilled over all requests, and for `qwen35` the preemptions.

  the xe driver's hwmon files; no root), its power limit and package temperature. The total is
  also in the top bar. Read-only: the launcher does not change power limits.

## Keys

| key | does |
| --- | --- |
| `↑` `↓` / `j` `k`, PgUp PgDn, Home End | move |
| `Enter` | edit: a popup for choices and suggestions, a line editor for the rest; fold a group |
| `←` `→` / `h` `l` | previous / next choice (or suggestion) in place; fold / unfold a group |
| `Space` | toggle on / off, next choice |
| `e` (F2) | type a custom value; `Tab` completes paths, `Ctrl-U` clears, `Esc` cancels |
| `d` / `D` | this setting / every setting back to the default of `start-server.sh` |
| `u` | undo |
| `/` | find a setting by name, key or flag; with no name match it searches the help text |
| `m` | the model list |
| `p` | settings files: `server.env` and the profiles; `n` saves the current values as a new profile, `x` deletes one |
| `s` / `S` | save to the open file / save as (`server.env`, a profile, a new profile) |
| `r` (F5) | launch, after the checks |
| `x` | stop the server (SIGTERM; after 5 s of stopping, `x` offers SIGKILL) |
| `Tab`, `1` `2` | switch screens |
| `?` | keys |
| `q` | quit; with unsaved changes it asks first. A running server keeps running |

## Files

- `server.env` (repo root): what `scripts/start-server.sh` reads. Saving writes only the settings
  that differ from the script's defaults, updates them in place and keeps comments and other
  lines; a setting set back to its default is removed from the file.
- `profiles/NAME.env`: named settings files in the same format (`p` to open, `n` to create).
  `scripts/start-server.sh` reads one with `SERVE_ENV=profiles/NAME.env`.
- `build/launch/`: `launch.env` (the values of the last launch, every setting written out),
  `server.log` (its output; the one before is `server.log.1`), `server.pid`, `preview.env`.

`r` first checks, and shows each check: the server binary is built, the model is a checkpoint
the engine serves, every setting is valid (a `qwen35` context must fit the checkpoint's
`max_position_embeddings`, it has no YaRN yet; `qwen38` goes past it), the port is free, no Docker container holds the cards
(skipped for the stub engine), and whether unsaved values are being launched (they are launched
as shown; the file is not changed). It refuses while any `xenithium-server` runs.

## Where the settings come from

script or docs have and the schema does not still appears, as text under "Other"; `--check` and
the `launch` gate (`xenithium-test-launch`) report any mismatch between the three. Adding or
renaming a `server.env` setting therefore also means a line in `schema()`.

## Code

`tools/launch/`: `term` (terminal: raw mode, alternate screen, diff rendering, key and mouse
decoding; no curses), `settings` (catalog, env files, validation, model scan), `proc` (dry run,
spawn, process and port checks, Docker, me

# Rounds

Round notes by model; each folder carries its own index + backlog (`README.md`) and
`NN-<topic>.md` notes:

- `qwen38-flash-next/` — qwen38, the main model (Flash-Next MoE); engine rounds 00-76 and 102+ (round 102: the
  served checkpoint is `qwen38-w4a16`; the KV page pool for qwen38, engine-wide `BatchEngine` admission now live for it).
  Round 122: the GDN projections as int4, opt-in (`XEN_GDN_W4`; engine-wide: `DenseSpec::Store::w4r`,
  `kernels::quantize_w4_row`, `gdn_decode` / `gdn_rows` take each matrix W4 or int8; `xenithium-bake gdn4-calib`).
  Round 123: backlog 190 (the dense model's GsPre, shared kernel) closed on micro tests; qwen38 int4 draft rows not adopted.
- `qwen38-27b/` — qwen35, the dense Qwen3.8-27B; rounds 01-34 (ids continue the main backlog; round 25 = engine round
  101, the host tail of sampled decode steps, engine-wide: `core::Sampler`, `core::BatchEngine`, both archs' logits copy;
  round 26 = engine round 114, experiments: int4 lm_head, the s4 W4 layout, W4A8 prefill; engine-wide: `kernels::W4Pack`,
  `DenseStore` packs w4 matrices by it, the W4 GEMMs read both layouts; backlog 202-204; round 27 = engine round 115: the
  W4A8 keep set and ablation, `xenithium-evalrun`, the s4 layout removed again (W4A8 stages the nib blocks); backlog
  205-209; round 28 = engine round 116: the two-stage lm_head, engine-wide kernels `kernels::head_select_tiles` (exact
  top-T 16-column tiles per row) and `kernels::dense_gemm_tiles` (the int8 / bf16 dense GEMM's bits on listed tiles),
  usable by qwen38's backlog 135; backlog 205 / 209 closed); round 29 = engine round 117: fast gates, engine-wide build fix
  (no-op builds relinked every SYCL binary: `CMAKE_LINK_DEPENDS_USE_LINKER OFF`, parallel device-code link jobs) and
  `scripts/gate-dumps.sh` (8-row teacher-forced dumps, numerics cases on one load); round 30 = engine round 118: backlog
  208 (split chunk with overlapped prefill sums) closed on micro tests, no engine change; round 31 = engine round 120: the
  lever-investigation plan part 2, engine-wide: `BatchEngine::kDepthMax` 7, the GDN core's uncached S write-back (both archs),
  `kernels::rms_norm_q8` + `w4a16_pf_a8_input`. Round 119 (qwen38-flash-next/119-prefill-a8-per-row.md) is part 1. Round 32 = engine round 121: sampling candidates from the
  cards (engine-wide: `kernels::head_cand_tiles`, `arch::HeadCands`, `StepModel::cand_tiles` / `logits_cands`, `core::Sampler::prepare_cands`,
  `core::BatchEngine::cands_for`; both archs). Round 33 = engine round 124: W4A8 prefill as the dense model's served default
  (`XEN_PREFILL_W4=a8`) and the pipelined W4A8 GEMM body in `w4a16_rows.cpp` (engine-wide kernel library, used only under
  W4A8, same bits). Round 34 = engine round 125: int8 q.k in the prefill attention (`gqa_attn_fa` qk 1 / 2 in
  the shared kernel library, `XEN_PREFILL_ATTN` int8 / int8-fast, fast on hi + lo int8 q; qwen35 only, opt-in). Round 35 =
  engine round 126: TP1, the dense model on one card (`--tp` / `--card`; engine-wide: a fabric of one device with a named
  error past the visible devices, the head's tile selection per vocabulary half, `kernels::w4a16_ksplit_for`; the launcher's
  TP settings per arch, `XEN_Q38_TP` / `XEN_Q38_CARD` for qwen38, TP2 only until backlog 214).

Engine-wide changes made for a model get a row here pointing into its folder.
